title: Precisely controlled visual stimulation to study experience-dependent neural plasticity in Xenopus tadpoles
protocol: Electroporate retinal ganglion cells.
Ablate one optic tectal lobe to induce convergence of inputs from both eyes onto the remaining tectal lobe.
Stimulate the left eye independently.
Stimulate the right eye independently.
Sequence the stimulation of the left and right eyes to control activity in convergent RGCs.
Anesthetize animals by placing them in 0.02% MS-222 at 22°C–25°C for less than 1 minute.
Transfer the anesthetized animal to Steinberg solution immediately after it stops moving.
Make an incision in the skin beneath the eyeball for inserting the anode behind the eye.
Centrifuge the plasmid solution at 20,000 × g for 5 min.
Take the supernatant and make a solution containing 0.5 μg/μl p α-actinin:GAL4/UAS:TdTomato and 0.25 μg/μl pUAS:Synaptophysin-GFP.
Add Fast Green (0.01% final) to monitor the solution during injection.
Load a glass pipette with the plasmid solution.
Attach the pipette to the Picospritzer.
Break the glass pipette tip by gently touching it with a Kimwipe.
Test the pipette by applying 90 psi pressure for 100 ms.
Hold the eyeball with forceps to prevent rotation.
Pierce the skin over the eye at the border between the lens and the retina with a glass pipette.
Inject plasmid solution into the eye until the blue color of the solution is visible inside the eye.
Insert an anode through the incision underneath the eye and position its tip behind the retina.
Place a cathode gently on top of the eye without pushing out the solution.
Apply a single electric pulse (52 V, 1.6 ms).
Transfer the tadpole into fresh Steinberg solution after electroporation.
Wait 24 hours after electroporation.
Anesthetize an animal in 0.02% MS-222 in Steinberg Solution.
Transfer the animal into Steinberg solution.
Make an incision at the center of the dorsal surface of the midbrain.
Cut the entire anterior-posterior extent of the midbrain.
Simultaneously cut both optic nerves at the optic chiasma.
Cut the boundary between the right half of the midbrain and the hindbrain.
Extend the incision to the ventral aspect of the midbrain.
Cut at the anterior edge of the optic tectum.
Pull a glass capillary and attach it to the microcapillary holder.
Break the tip to make an 100 μm diameter opening.
Connect the tube to a vacuum line.
Suck out the right tectal lobe and tegmentum.
Transfer the tadpole to fresh Steinberg solution.
Maintain the animals at 18°C for 20–24 hours.
Move the animals to an incubator at 22°C.
Never expose animals to MS222 after surgery.
Set an animal on a Sylgard block with a hole carved in the Sylgard to hold the tadpole comfortably.
Add a few drops of Steinberg’s solution and place a coverslip over the tadpole.

Use a regular fluorescent microscope or a spinning disc confocal microscope (ex, Perkin Elmer/Yokogawa CSU-X1) with a 20× objective lens to identify animals in which one or a few labeled RGC axons project to the single ipsilateral tectal lobe.
Provide visual stimulation to one eye.
Prevent indirect activation of the other eye by providing persistent illumination.
Stimulate one eye with masking light and provide a light OFF stimulus to the other eye.
Dim LEDs instead of turning them off completely when generating an off stimulus.
Set the visual stimulator using the specified configuration table.
Push key#7 on the circuit board to start the stimulation program.
Push key#8 on the circuit board to stop and reset the program.
Connect the circuit board to a 12 V AC adaptor.
Connect the wires from the tadpole stimulation chamber to the circuit board.
Turn on the two toggle switches at the left corner.
Push key#2 and set dt to “15” ([ms] interval between left and right eyes).
Set u to “1024” (light ON intensity for right LED, maximum setting) by pushing key#3 and key#5/6.
Set d to “192” (light OFF intensity for right LED) by pushing key#4 and key#5/6.
Long push key#2 until it is set at “1024” (light ON intensity of left LED).
Set D to “192” (light ON intensity of left LED) by long pushing key#3 and key#5/6.
Set I to “11” ([s] cycle time interval) by pushing key#1 and key#5/6.
Long push key#4 until p is set at “1” (ramp speed).
Long push key#7 until “10 h” is displayed (stimulation time).
Push key#7 to start stimulation.
Select a chamber where the gap between the acrylic plates fits the width of the tadpole.
Support the anterior part of the animal with a Sylgard block.
Support the tail of the animal using Sylgard strips.
Cover the dorsal side of the animal with a coverslip.
Attach the coverslip to the acrylic plate with utility wax.
Introduce drugs into the bath solution according to the experimental design.
Place animals in the stimulation chamber.
Put the chamber in a light-tight black container with about 150 mL capacity.
Fill the container with 50 mL Steinberg solution.
Stimulate the right eye with dimming light (from maximum illumination to complete off, 20% change /s in the turn on period, 5.5 s/stimulation cycle).
Stimulate the left eye with persistent light at 100% luminance.
Continue stimulation for 5 min.
Add 50 mL of 4 μM MK801 in Steinberg’s solution to the chamber to achieve a final concentration of 2 μM MK801.
Continue the stimulation protocol for 14 min.
After 15 min total exposure, turn off the stimulation and immediately pour 50 mL of fresh Steinberg's solution into the chamber to dilute the MK801 rapidly.
Drain all the MK801 solution from the chamber.
Replace with 50 mL of fresh Steinberg’s solution.
Wash the chamber three more times with 50 mL of fresh Steinberg solution.
Set the controller for both eyes at a luminance range of 100%–18.8%, with each stimulation cycle lasting 11 seconds, and continue the duration for 8 hours.
Start the visual stimulation when 15 min have passed after turning off the LED.
Collect time-lapse images of the axons at intervals from 1 to 24 hours, depending on the experimental design.
Quantify branch dynamics in axon arbor morphology to demonstrate directed growth.
Image samples at shorter intervals, such as every 1-2 hours over 4-8 hours, for detailed analysis.
Collect time-lapse images with a spinning disc microscope or multiphoton microscope immediately before visual stimulation.
